candidates.title: A provider key or billing refusal fails every in-flight room build for good; only a per-job operator command reopens them
candidates.journey_step: C.3 Reconstruction (World Labs) and C.2 preparation (Gemini, SAM, OpenAI)
evidence: pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/website_atlas_preview.py:315-320 a 'cannot succeed' code -> state failed now; 'an operator's retry reopens the job after a fix'

candidates.today: An expired or rotated API key (401), an unpaid provider account (402) or a revoked permission (403) is treated as 'this request can never succeed'. Every job that hits it in that window ends failed at once. No alarm pages for failed jobs. After the key is fixed, an operator must reopen each job by hand with a door command. The site is never told why; its job ends when the 7-day window sweep runs.
candidates.should: A refusal about Blueprint's own credentials or account is an outage: it pages once and the jobs wait and resume by themselves once the key works.
candidates.proposal: In job_retry_policy, move 401 and 402 (and 403 when the provider body names the key or account) to the outage class that _outage_retry already handles until the job's deadline, and page once per provider on the first such refusal. One small PR plus tests.
candidates.user_result: After a key rotation, jobs finish on their own instead of ending; no per-job operator command.
candidates.risk: A genuine 403 for a forbidden request would be retried until the job window ends; the retries cost nothing because the provider refuses before work. Paid admission still applies to each retry.
candidates.requirement_source: job_retry_policy (AGENTS.md: one retry rule); the per-job reopen requirement has source nobody, and doctrine forbids an operator command as the only way forward

candidates.today: Doctrine says never make a deploy or an operator command the only way to retry. Today these states have no other exit: a parked or failed room build (door --atlas-retry); an expired scene window (door extend-scene-execution-window, 9 intents now); a launch whose spend cannot be proven (settled by hand); a dead dispatcher (read the journal); a fault in Blueprint's code (a deploy before the window's last two hours); a preparation past six retries (waits for the window to end). None of the parked states pages, and the preparation recovery counter is not read by the alarm.
candidates.should: Each wait has a timed automatic retry up to the job's deadline, then one message to the site; operator commands only speed things up.
candidates.proposal: One PR per stage, smallest first: (a) Atlas: retry a parked job automatically once after each deploy (a release switch already does this since #3664); (b) preparation: after the six retries, keep retrying on the outage schedule until the grant ends; (c) let the stall alarm read .website_preparation_recovery_failures.json. Delete the execution-window extension as a requirement: when it expires the job ends with what it has, as the spending cap already does.
candidates.user_result: Jobs no longer wait on a person; the site hears an ending instead of silence.
candidates.risk: Automatic retries after a deploy may repeat a refusal; each step keeps its paid receipts, so nothing is bought twice.
candidates.requirement_source: doctrine (AGENTS.md: never make a deploy or an operator command the only way to retry) argues against each; the extension requirement cites an owner approval reference
